thread:
Anna: quick q — we're seeing persistent queueing on west1 GPU pools during peak. thinking about per-tenant backpressure strategies. options: strict per-tenant token buckets, per-route queues, priority queues with aging, or keep single FIFO and rely on autoscale. thoughts?
Mike: +1 to discussing. current autoscale adds capacity too slowly for short spikes, so queues fill and latency spikes.
Priya: main goals: 1) protect SLOs for paid tiers 2) avoid noisy-tenant stomping 3) keep operational complexity manageable.
Diego: customer POV — paid tiers expect stable latency. fallback behavior matters: do we fail fast, queue, or route to cheaper model?
Li: a few mid-market customers asked for "guaranteed calls" during spikes. they'd accept higher $ for reserved tokens.
Kevin: sketch: per-tenant token_bucket + a small priority queue. token_bucket enforces long-term rate; queue absorbs short bursts; priority decides between SLA tiers. aging prevents starvation.
Anna: love that. what's complexity of enforcement? per-GPU pool accounting? global?
Mike: cheapest to implement at routing layer: maintain token state per-tenant per-pool (shards by pool id). global fairness requires cross-pool coordination which is heavier (consistent hashing + periodic sync).
Priya: can we do hybrid: per-pool buckets + a global budget for emergencies? e.g., if pool saturated, consult global fallback budget to allow limited cross-pool bursts.
Kevin: yes. rough config example we prototyped:
```yaml
venues:
  - pool: west1-a
    per_tenant_bucket:
      refill_rate: 5rps
      burst: 20
    priority_levels:
      - name: enterprise
        weight: 10
      - name: standard
        weight: 1
    queue_length: 200
    aging_ms: 5000
global:
  emergency_budget: 100rps
  fallback_model: llama-guest-1
```
Priya: few notes: queue_length per-pool prevents OOMs and keeps fairness local. aging_ms slowly increases effective priority for long-waiting requests.
Diego: how do we present this in product? suggest: "Reserved tokens" for enterprise + "Best effort" for standard. Also an opt-in cross-region fallback.
Li: customers want metrics: tokens consumed, drops, avg queue time. please make them easy to surface in Console.
autoscale-bot: [alert] west1-a pool CPU/GPU util 96% for 00:12:34 — autoscale delta pending.
Mike: ops cost angle: per-tenant buckets increase memory and bookkeeping. if we have 10k tenants, per-pool state could be heavy. need TTL eviction for inactive tenants.
Anna: on billing — do we charge for queued time or only execution tokens?
Diego: recommend charging on execution tokens only; but we can charge for "reserved tokens" pre-purchases. queued time should be visible as SLA-impact metric, not billable.
Kevin: fallback behavior ideas: 1) degrade to smaller model with lower cost 2) respond with 429 + retry-after 3) best-effort queue with timeout and clear error if timed out. mix-and-match per-tenant policy.
Priya: operationally prefer deterministic outcomes: for reserved tenants, try cross-pool first, then degrade model, then queue. for best-effort, queue then 429.
Anna: can we simulate outcomes before rollout? e.g., replay production request traces into a local capacity simulator to calculate percent orders that would be queued/dropped under configs.
Mike: yes — we have traces. we should run a sweep of 3 configs: FIFO-only, per-tenant buckets + queue, and priority-queue-with-aging across trace. produces expected latencies, drops, and cross-pool transfers. low-effort POC.
Diego: timeline? customers will want a timeframe for reserved tokens feature.
Anna: propose: POC sim + small runtime POC in canary cluster (west1-b) over 2 weeks, then public beta.
Li: can we include a self-serve UI for reserved tokens in Console beta? even a form with limits will help customer sales calls.
Priya: alerting considerations: new alerts for bucket exhaustion rate, queue length spikes, cross-pool transfer rate. also add regression checks to Ensure we don't increase p99 tail.
Kevin: agree. one more config snippet: token bucket enforcement pseudocode:
```
if tenant.tokens >= 1:
  tenant.tokens -= 1
  allow()
else if queue.length < cfg.queue_length:
  queue.push(req, priority=tenant.priority, ts=now)
else:
  reject(429)
```
Anna: ok next steps: 1) Mike & Kevin run trace sim of 3 configs (3 days) 2) Priya defines SRE alerting thresholds 3) Product/CS (Diego+Li) craft billing + Console flow 4) small canary POC in west1-b after sim results.
Diego: fine. I'll draft customer messaging.
Mike: starting trace job now. linking job id: trace-run-20260318-01
Anna: thanks all. @autoscale-bot can you post an hourly summary of pool saturation for the next 48h into #eng-platform? would help tune thresholds. :thumbsup:
autoscale-bot: will do — hourly summaries enabled for eng-platform.
